results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 54 aligned units match their spec controlling_idea in the same order; loosest matches are p25 (outline gives the freshness table's general point, spec the one-rhythm consequence) and p18 (outline leads with the OMS, spec with the missing owner of the cross-context view), both the same idea.
Mirrors check 1: the spec-blind outline lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as sections[].paragraphs[].

The outliner flagged no unit. Entity-Owner Table ¶1 (deliverable, two term definitions, scope) was examined: the definitions and scope serve the single idea of presenting the table. No unit carries two ideas.

Every body unit ties to the supporting claim its section declares (S1 scene and truth patterns; S2 definitions; S3 contexts; S4 table; S5 four ways and stages; S2/S4 suite and In Practice; S6 When It Goes Wrong); intro and conclusion units frame or apply the thesis.

Each table, quotation and scenario has an adjacent statement of what it shows (e.g. 'as the table shows, each answer was true of a different number'; 'Its point is that...'; 'one writer per entity, enforced by the plumbing'; 'Read these as vendors explaining their own categories'); figure captions state their point.

All 53 declared transitions are expressed, by a connective sentence or by parallel bold run-in labels (the four ways, the five failure modes, Established / Depends on context / The author's synthesis). Weakest but passing: p03 (roadmap opens without picking up 'the decisions'), the Entity-Owner Table opening (culmination carried only by 'The deliverable of this chapter' and the reused terms record, write, copies), and the conclusion (heading only).

results.finding: The label W5 is used twice in the Truth-patterns table and is never introduced; W1 and W2 were each given as 'Waypoint decision W1/W2' with their content, W5 was not, and the two cells attach it to two different things (refund flow, price source).

Apart from W5 (failed separately), acronyms are expanded where first used (WMS, ERP, POS, OMS, PIM, SKU, GTIN, EDI, B2B, PSP, D2C, 3PL), event and reconciliation are defined before the table that uses them, and named incidents are glossed on first appearance. 'Omnichannel stage' and the named failure patterns are in the audience's prior knowledge.

(a) The reader's principle (case, concepts, tool, choices, case resolved, failures) agrees with the declared problem_solution flow and its prerequisite ordering. (b) No section position marked unclear. (c) All eight lost-thread items verified against the draft and ruled NOT MATERIAL: forward reference to the stage table is explicit and 'omnichannel stage' is known to the audience; named incidents are each glossed where they first appear; the repeated ERP expansion is a true redundancy but a minor irritation; the heading's 'It' has no referent (the heading is the spec's own) but the section's first sentence states its subject; 'Public examples' is a labelled paragraph, an interruption of expectation only; the Secret Agent sentence itself says why it is there and the audience knows the catalogue; the two lists of five are separated by an explicit 'never decided' / 'decided is not kept' boundary, and the reader described both sections correctly; W5 is truly never introduced but does not interrupt the argument (recorded as the known_before_new fail). (e) Moving Truth Patterns earlier and moving Public examples after the replay are answered by the top-level flow rationale and the In Practice large_to_small rationale; putting Scale Stages directly after Four Ways with the suite section last is not answered by any rationale (the spec only says the three stay together).
The introduction opens on a concrete puzzling scenario, states the claim and gives a specific roadmap; none of the five patterns applies.
The conclusion is sorted into established, context-dependent and the author's judgement, then questions and a hand-off; no new subtopic, no body evidence beyond source tags, not a bare restatement.

'Write the entity–owner table before buying any hub... a bought OMS fed by four unreconciled order sources is a fifth copy' is stated in no single section and delivers the spec's so_what. The spec's framing of 'one decision seen four ways' is not put in those words.
The conclusion returns to the opening parcel: 'neither status was stale, each was true of its own object, and what was missing was an owner of the view across them.'

The cold reader predicted all expected elements in the right order (six answers, vocabulary, meanings of 'order', entity–owner table, ownership comparison, return to Kestrel & Pine's stock, the two kinds of failure) with vendor documentation as evidence. Mispredictions, not material: guessed the comparison would be organised by growth stage (it is four ways, then suites, then stages) and expected no citations (Evans and Fowler appear).

The cold answer asks first which system is the record, then which apps, jobs or people can write stock in the shop besides the refresh; it never asks how to sync faster. The writer question is folded into 'how did the copy get to 12' beside a staleness check, and names writers in the shop only.
The cold answer says yes, each 'order' is a different object sharing an order number, and that what is missing is one owner of the view across them, as expected.
The cold answer fills record, writer, copies, how copies learn and how disagreement is found for consumer price, each specifically and consistent with the draft's table row.
